To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the multiple imputation method appears to be a valid approach for the analysis of the missing food intake data in the GISSi-Prevenzione case study.
the multiple imputation approach was the most effective method for dealing with missing data in the analysis of the benefits of the Mediterranean diet in the GISS I-Prevenzione trial.

the use of multiple imputation methods for handling missing data can provide valid estimates, preserving the observed data distributions and relationships between the variables, and that this is especially true when the missingness mechanism is not missing at random, as in the case of the food intake frequencies of the GISSI Prevenzione study.

the analysis of missing values from a large cohort study of cardiovascular risk factors.
the analysis of missing values in the context of a case-control study of the Mediterranean diet.

the Mediterranean diet is beneficial to the health of the population, but that the benefits are more pronounced in those individuals who have a higher intake of fish, legumes and fruits, and a lower intake of meat, and that the benefits are not restricted to cardiovascular disease but extend to all causes of mortality and morbidity.
MI is an effective and valid method for handling the problem of missing values in epidemiological studies.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of a Mediterranean diet, the MI method is the most appropriate for handling the missing data problem.

the use of MI in the GISSi-Prevenzione data set produced results that were more consistent with the observed data and with the theoretical expectations of a randomised trial, and that the use of the complete data or of simple imputation methods produced results that were less consistent with the observed and theoretical data.
the results from the MI analyses were similar to those obtained with complete data and that the imputation methods used did not introduce bias in the estimates of the effects of interest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MI is a powerful tool for handling missing data in the analysis of repeated measurements.

MI is a powerful and flexible tool for handling missing data in epidemiologic studies, and that it should be considered as a first option for the analysis of epidemiologic data with a high rate of missing values.
MI can be used in epidemiology and in particular for the analysis of dietary intake data.
